newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EXPANSION, SERVICES MAKE MATAV EFFICIENT - ING BARINGS.
newsitem.headline: EXPANSION, SERVICES MAKE MATAV EFFICIENT - ING BARINGS.

text.p: Hungarian telecommunications company Matav Rt, a candidate for a later bourse listing, may turn into an attractive telecom company amid continuous expansion of its business, ING Barings said in a company report.

"The steady expansion of the telecom network, coupled with an increasing number of new services and a decrease in staff may gradually make Matav an efficient and prosperous telecom company," analyst Gergely Varkonyi said.
The report compared Matav to SPT Telekom of the Czech Republic and Slovak Telecom of Slovakia and said it was better on an operating level but was worse in terms of profitability.

"Matav outperforms these regional telecom companies mainly at an operational level (in terms of revenues per line, revenues per employee) but is outperformed in terms of profitability," Varkonyi said.
Matav's revenues per line was $565, whereas it was $417 for SPT Telekom and $275 for Slovak Telekom.
Revenues per employee were $46,633 for Matav, $38,126 for SPT Telekom and $20,312 for Slovak Telekom.
However, Matav generated $1,268 in net profit per employee, remaining well below $6,969 by SPT Telekom and and $4,569 by Slovak Telekom. These figures were calculated by 1995 data.
The report said that Matav's lower profitability was understandable given that Hungary used to have one of the most underdeveloped telecom networks in Europe.
Matav is 67 percent owned by MagyarCom, a 50-50 percent consortium of Deutsche Telekom and Ameritech , while the rest is held by a variety of investors.
This consortium became responsible for organising an IPO and floating Matav shares on both the Budapest Stock Exchange and on the New York Stock Exchange not later than 1999, ING Barings said.
"This IPO will probably take place in late 1997 or early 1998," Varkonyi said.
The company has said only that it has chosen Merrill Lynch as adviser for a possible IPO.
